newsitem.title: USA: EU fin mins told G7 euro would come on time-Silguy.
newsitem.headline: EU fin mins told G7 euro would come on time-Silguy.

text.p: European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Friday that European finance ministers told their G7 partners they were determined to launch the euro in time on January 1, 1999.
"There was a unanimous determination from the Europeans to say that the Euro will be launched on January 1, 1999," he told reporters after a meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers here.
"On the American side, there were no questions about either the date or the (Maastricht Treaty) criteria," he added.
"For them it's a done deal," de Silguy said.
The ministers from France and Germany also said their countries would be ready for the launch of the single currency.

The arrival of a new socialist-led government in France and political and economic problems in Germany have raised fears the two countries might overshoot a Maastricht Treaty criterion calling for deficits to be reduced to no more than three percent of gross domestic product.
"The French and the Germans said they would be ready for January 1, 1999," he said.
De Silguy said that the discussion on Europe had mostly focussed on the need for structural reform to reduce the continent's high unemployment rate.

G7 ministers -- from Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- also looked at measures being taken to reduce instability on financial markets which would arise from the launch of the euro.
The best guarantee against this was continuing efforts to bring national economies into line with the convergence criteria in the Maastricht Treaty, de Silguy said.
He added that Europe should give an indication to financial markets as to how it planned to fix exchange rates ahead of the launch of the euro.
"I tend to think that one should fix either the method or the rates by the time we decide the list of countries joining the single currency at the latest."
EU countries are due to decide in spring 1998 which countries will qualify for EMU in 1999.
